question: A 28-year-old woman is referred for a pelvic ultrasound to assess a suspected ovarian cyst. The sonographer requires optimal pelvic views. Which preparation instruction is MOST appropriate?

answers.text: Fast for 6 hours before the scan to reduce bowel gas.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Fasting is appropriate for upper abdominal scans (gallbladder, liver). For transabdominal pelvic ultrasound, a FULL BLADDER is required — it acts as an acoustic window and displaces overlying bowel gas.

answers.text: Drink 1 litre of water 1 hour before the scan and do not void until after the scan.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Transabdominal pelvic ultrasound requires a full urinary bladder. The filled bladder acts as an acoustic window that allows sound waves to pass into the pelvis and displaces gas-filled bowel loops that would otherwise obscure the uterus and ovaries.

answers.text: Void immediately before the scan so the bladder is empty for clearest views.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. An empty bladder is preferred only for transvaginal ultrasound. For transabdominal pelvic scanning, the bladder must be full to provide an acoustic window to the pelvis.

answers.text: No specific preparation is needed for pelvic ultrasound.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A full urinary bladder is mandatory preparation for transabdominal pelvic ultrasound. Without it, overlying bowel gas will obscure pelvic structures and the scan will be non-diagnostic.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review pelvic ultrasound preparation. A full urinary bladder is required for transabdominal pelvic scanning because it serves as an acoustic window and displaces overlying bowel gas.
Correct. For transabdominal pelvic ultrasound, a full bladder is essential — it provides the acoustic window to the pelvis.
